_note: What the head coach says in his own words (GDD 4.9.2, session C3; read by CoachTalk, scripts/core/coach_talk.gd). Three uses: (1) the Sunday-evening WEEK TALK (last week in a few lines from the day log, this week explained from the season plan: phase, why the key sessions, one thing to focus on; it always stops Play week, user 2026-10-11), (2) the MESSAGE after a race (the facts, the coach's Race-story line in his own words from coaches.json, a closing line), (3) the coach's WHY line in the day editor. His COMMUNICATION attribute sets the detail (detail.short_max / full_min: short = 'Do it.', normal, full = he explains why); his personality (coaches.json voice: calm / drill / warm / tactician) sets the voice. Placeholders in a text are filled by the code: {name} (the athlete's first name), {coach_first}, {done}, {planned}, {n}, {meet}, {result}, {phase}, {week}, {weeks}, {weekday}, {session}, {why}, {short}, {areas}, {area}, {injury}, {days}. Topics (the 0-2 questions with replies) are storylets in data/storylets/week_talk.json. Texts only here, never in scripts.

phase.general_base: Keep the easy runs easy. Don't turn them into races.
phase.indoor_specific: Run the intervals evenly. The last rep should not be much slower than the first.
phase.spring_base: Build steadily. This is where the summer is made.
phase.pre_competition: Sharpen the speed, but stay fresh enough to enjoy it.
phase.race_season: Recover well between races. Sleep, food, easy days.
phase.transition: Switch off a little. Run for fun this week.
phase.autumn_general: Start gently. There is a whole year ahead.

focus.default: Show up, do the work, and tell me how it feels.

phase_why.general_base: This phase builds the engine. The training is easy on purpose: it makes everything later possible.
phase_why.indoor_specific: The indoor target is close, so we add race-pace work and sharpen up.
phase_why.spring_base: Back to building before the outdoor season: tempo, hills and strength.
phase_why.pre_competition: Racing is near. Speed work now makes the first outdoor races sharp.
phase_why.race_season: Racing season. We keep the speed, race, and recover well in between.
phase_why.transition: Easy weeks to rest the body and the mind after the summer.
phase_why.autumn_general: A gentle start to the new training year.

easy_run.why: Easy running builds your aerobic base without tiring you. Keep it relaxed.

long_run.why: A long run teaches your body to keep going. Keep the pace easy.

fartlek.why: Fartlek mixes fast and slow running. It builds speed and stamina without a strict watch.

tempo_run.why: A tempo run at steady hard effort raises the pace you can hold.

intervals_800.why: Intervals at race pace teach your body the 800 m. Keep the reps even.

speed_strides.why: Short fast strides keep your legs quick without tiring you.

hill_sprints.why: Hill sprints build power and speed. Short and hard, with full rests.

start_practice.why: Start practice makes the first 100 metres automatic.

club_session.why: The group session pushes you with others. Run with them, not ahead of them.

strength.why: Strength and core work makes you robust and your stride stronger.

drills.why: Running drills fix your technique. Slow, precise, no rushing.

mobility.why: Mobility keeps you supple and helps you recover.

xc_skiing.why: Skiing builds your engine with little pounding on the legs.

aqua_jog.why: Running in water keeps the fitness while the legs rest.

stationary_bike.why: The bike keeps the engine going without pounding the legs.

swimming.why: Swimming is a gentle full-body session that helps you recover.

gym_core.why: Core and upper-body work keeps you strong while the legs rest.

day.title: COACH
day.race: Race day. Warm up properly, run your own race.

profile.range_note: You have worked with him for {weeks} weeks, so these are estimates. After {need} weeks you know him well.
profile.exact_note: After {weeks} weeks together you know him well.

explain.style: How he leads. A supportive coach asks and encourages; a controlling one tells you what to do. Neither is wrong, but some athletes need the one more than the other.
explain.demands: Which of the coach's three season plans he leans towards: Steady plays it safe, Ambitious wants more.
explain.fit: How your temperament and his character go together. It shows after four weeks. You click, it is fine, or there is some friction. It moves how much you trust him.
explain.trust: How much you trust each other. It grows when you listen to him and do well, and falls when you ignore him. A strong bond makes him explain more.

open: Sunday evening, {name}. Let's look at the week together.
Sit down a moment, {name}. The week is done.

comment.injured: The injury comes first. Nothing else matters until it is better.
comment.exhausted: You were running on empty. That is not strength, it is a warning.
comment.tired: Your legs were heavy. That is normal, but watch it.
comment.fresh: You are fresh. Good. We can ask a little more.
comment.kept: You kept the rhythm all week. That is how it grows.
comment.missed: A few sessions went missing. It happens. We keep the rhythm.
comment.none: A week without training. The body rests, but we start again soon.
comment.sore: Some soreness. Not a problem yet, but listen to it.
comment.race_pb: A personal best. Calm running, and it paid.
comment.race_good: A good race. I was glad to see how relaxed you were.
comment.race_bad: The race was below you. We look at it without hurry.
comment.race_hurt: After a race like that, rest comes first.

day.easy: Easy means easy. Breathe and relax.
day.hard: Today asks for effort. Stay relaxed inside it.
day.rest: Rest day. Recovery is part of the work.

race.pb: Walk it out, and rest tomorrow.
race.good: Good running. Eat, drink, and sleep well tonight.
race.bad: Don't worry about it tonight. Sleep, eat, and we look at it together.
race.hurt: Rest first. We will talk when you have recovered.

open: Right, {name}. Week's done. Straight to it.

comment.injured: You're hurt, so you do exactly what the limits say. No heroics.
comment.exhausted: You're empty. That's what too much looks like. Back off.
comment.tired: Heavy legs. Good, that means you worked.
comment.fresh: You're fresh. No excuses, then. We push.
comment.kept: Every session done. That's the standard.
comment.missed: Sessions missing. That's not the standard.
comment.none: A whole week off. That's a problem.
comment.sore: You're sore. Tell me before it becomes an injury.
comment.race_pb: Personal best. Good. Don't get comfortable.
comment.race_good: A decent race. We want more.
comment.race_bad: That race was below you. I expect more.
comment.race_hurt: You went down. Get up, rest, then we go again.

day.easy: Easy means easy. Don't turn it into a race.
day.rest: Rest day. Rest properly. That's an order.

race.good: Fine. Eat and sleep. Monday we work.
race.bad: Not good enough. We fix it in training.
race.hurt: Get checked if it hurts. Don't be stupid about it.

open: Hi {name}, come sit. Let's talk about the week.
Sunday evening, {name}. How are you doing?

comment.injured: I'm sorry about the injury. We take it slowly and you will be back.
comment.exhausted: You were so tired. You don't have to be a hero, you know.
comment.tired: Your legs were heavy, I could see it. Be kind to yourself.
comment.fresh: You look fresh and happy. I like that.
comment.kept: You did every session! I'm proud of you.
comment.missed: A few sessions missed, and that's all right. Life happens.
comment.none: A week off. Rest is allowed, you know.
comment.sore: A little soreness. Tell me if it grows, all right?
comment.race_pb: A personal best! I'm so proud of you!
comment.race_good: A lovely race. You should be happy.
comment.race_bad: It wasn't your day, and that's all right. We go again.
comment.race_hurt: Oh, that was a rough one. Rest and be kind to yourself.

close: I'm proud of you. See you on Monday!

day.easy: An easy day is a good day. Enjoy it.
day.hard: A tough one today, but you can do it.
day.rest: A rest day! Do something nice.

race.pb: Celebrate a little tonight. You deserve it.
race.good: You ran so nicely. Rest up and enjoy it.
race.bad: Don't be hard on yourself. One race is only one race.
race.hurt: Take care of yourself first. Everything else can wait.

open: Sunday, {name}. Let's go through the numbers.

comment.injured: The injury changes the plan. We adapt; that is what plans are for.
comment.exhausted: Your fatigue was too high. The data says back off.
comment.tired: Fatigue was high late in the week. Expected after this load.
comment.fresh: Your fatigue was low. We have room for more.
comment.kept: Full compliance with the plan. Good data.
comment.missed: Sessions missed, so less stimulus than planned. We adjust.
comment.none: No training, no stimulus. We restart it.
comment.sore: There was soreness. Watch the trend, not one day.
comment.race_pb: A personal best. The splits will show where it came from.
comment.race_good: A good result for your level. The race was read well.
comment.race_bad: Worse than the numbers predicted. The race wasn't read right. We look at it.
comment.race_hurt: A race with a fall or an injury tells us little. Recover first.

close: Ask if you want the details.

day.easy: Easy keeps your recovery on track.
day.hard: A quality session. The pace matters more than the volume.
day.rest: Rest day. Adaptation happens in the rest.

race.pb: Good data for the next plan. Recover tomorrow.
race.good: Solid. I'll look at the splits and tell you what I see.
race.bad: We will find the mistake. Not tonight; rest first.
race.hurt: No conclusions from this one. Recover, then we continue.
